title: Octopus ke 3 dil aur neela khoon!
source: Live Science · Smithsonian Magazine · Scientific American

captions.instagram:
Hey, want to hear something? How many hearts do you have? One, right?

Octopus ke 3 dil hote hain aur khoon neela! 🐙💙 Kyunki uske khoon mein lohe ki jagah TAANBA (copper) hota hai. Aur tairte waqt uska bada dil kuch pal ke liye ruk jaata hai!

Sources: Live Science, Smithsonian Magazine, Scientific American.

Verses:
• An octopus has three hearts — Live Science; Smithsonian
• Two (branchial) hearts pump blood through the gills; the larger systemic heart pumps it to the body — Live Science; Smithsonian
• Octopus blood is blue because its oxygen carrier, hemocyanin, uses copper (ours uses iron) — Smithsonian; Scientific American
• The systemic heart stops for a few moments when the octopus swims; this may be why it prefers crawling (reason not certain) — Live Science; Smithsonian

claims.claim: Two (branchial) hearts pump blood through the gills; the larger systemic heart pumps it to the body
Octopus blood is blue because its oxygen carrier, hemocyanin, uses copper (ours uses iron)
The systemic heart stops for a few moments when the octopus swims; this may be why it prefers crawling (reason not certain)

verify_note: Heart-stops-while-swimming: Live Science says no one is certain why; framed with 'शायद'.
